content:
Yara: Quick follow-up to the residency RFC. I sketched a 'consent-broker + dual-lease' variant that tries to reduce cross-region tail while keeping owner-authoritative guarantees. High level: a lightweight broker issues short dual-leases (local+owner) so proxies can decide fast. Thoughts?

Cal: What's a dual-lease? Sounds similar to handshake but different name.

Yara: Dual-lease = owner issues a short owner-lease and consent-broker mints a matching local-lease token that proxies can cache. The local region can accept writes while the owner-lease is active; owner still issues canonical ids. Broker coordinates epochs so revokes are immediate.

Diego: So flow: proxy asks broker -> broker returns {local_token, owner_lease_reference, epoch, ttl}. Proxy may accept local writes if token present. How do we avoid giving write power indefinitely?

Yara: TTL small (50ms-2s). Broker only issues tokens if owner confirms ability to reconcile backlog. Broker is aware of per-tenant mode: owner-only, dual-lease, eventual.

Leah: Where does the broker live? Is it centralized? Could be a small replicated control-plane service per region pair. Needs to be very low-latency and highly available.

Yara: We propose a distributed broker cluster per region pair (or per geo), with fast caching at proxies. Broker maintains epoch and token signing; tokens are HMAC-signed so proxies can verify without owner call.

Cal: DB invariants? Owner still mints canonical sequence numbers. Local writes get provisional ids and a broker token stamp. Reconciliation worker maps provisional->canonical, using the owner_lease_reference to correlate. Conflicts resolved by owner policy (owner wins, compensator jobs).

Diego: Revocation path? If owner changes or policy flips we need quick revoke.

Yara: Broker increments epoch and publishes revocation tombstones. Proxies drop tokens immediately on manifest refresh or revocation push. Broker also emits pubsub events for edge caches.

Leah: Telemetry: record `residency.path` (local-accepted, forwarded-sync, broker-denied, queued-eventual), `residency.token_hit`, `residency.reconcile_lag_ms`, `residency.forward_latency_ms`. Tag by tenant, region, and policy. Add alert if reconcile lag > X or conflict_rate > Y.

Cal: How is this better than cached consent tokens? Broker centralizes safety checks (backpressure, owner load) and can reduce unnecessary forward attempts by refusing tokens when owner is overloaded.

Diego: Failure modes: if broker is partitioned, proxies fall back to manifest-only decisions. We must design a safe default: if no token and mode==dual-lease, proxy either 1) sync-forward, or 2) if allowed by tenant -> provisional+enqueue.

Yara: Pseudo-proxy flow:
```
# proxy flow (simplified)
manifest = getTenantManifest(tenant)
if escrow.owner == local:
  commitLocal(); emit(metric:residency.path=local-owner)
  return 200
if manifest.mode == "owner-only": return 403
if manifest.mode == "dual-lease":
  token = localCache.getToken(tenant)
  if token && verify(token.epoch == manifest.epoch) {
    commitProvisional(token); emit(metric:residency.path=local-accepted)
    return 200
  }
  # try broker request with short timeout
  resp = broker.requestToken(tenant, timeout=100ms)
  if resp.ok { cacheToken(resp.token); commitProvisional(resp.token); return 200 }
  if manifest.allow_eventual { enqueueProvisional(); return 202 }
  # last resort: sync-forward with short timeout
  resp = forwardToOwner(timeout=250ms)
  if resp.ok { return 200 } else return 504
```

Leah: Timeouts are tunable per-tenant. High-SLA tenants get longer forward timeouts or forced sync-only.

Cal: Security: tokens signed and include tenant, epoch, broker_id, ttl; store broker state encrypted for PII tenants. All cross-region forwards and broker issuances generate audit events to tenant sink.

Diego: Canary plan: enable dual-lease for synthetic low-risk tenants between two regions. Gate on metrics: token_hit_rate, forwarded_p95, reconcile_lag_p50/p95, conflict_rate. Ops-bot run a sim before canary.

consent-bot: simulated run uploaded -> https://ci.redwood/sims/consent-broker/3799999999 (sim: 50k reqs/tenant, 45% writes, inter-region p95 220ms). With dual-lease token hit 55% simulated app p95 reduced ~38%.

Yara: Implementation owners suggested: broker service (Yara + eng-runtime), proxy token cache & flow (Cal + eng-platform), reconciliation worker (Diego + eng-sre), control-plane manifest + revocation fanout (product/infra).

Leah: Compliance: enforce KMS tags on broker entries for regulated tenants, require additional audit sinks and retention. Also add a policy flag that forbids dual-lease for specific tenants.

Cal: Agree to own proxy changes. Will add unit tests and integration test with broker sim.

Diego: I'll own reconciliation and compensator semantics. I'll prototype id-mapping queue and conflict handlers.

Yara: I'll design broker API: requestToken(tenant, desired_ttl, hint_owner) -> token | deny | wait. Will write sequence diagrams and token proto.

Leah: I'll coordinate canary + compliance gating. Let's try a small non-PII canary next week.

deploy-bot: artifacts + canary checklist available -> https://ci.redwood/canaries/consent-broker/3799999999 (includes sim results and pre-rollout safety checks)

Yara: Thanks folks. I'll draft RFC addendum and ping reviewers. :rocket:
